source.citation: Fukuchi RK, Fukuchi CA, Duarte M (2017). A public dataset of running biomechanics and the effects of running speed on lower extremity kinematics and kinetics. PeerJ 5:e3298
source.note: derived summary statistics from the raw marker and force files

method.model: sagittal seven-mass model, x forward, y up (plate = 0), metres: thigh, shank, foot of both legs plus one head-arms-trunk point mass; angular momentum H and COM per kg of body mass
method.joints: hip = Harrington 2007 pelvis-regression hip joint centre; knee = midpoint of Knee and Knee.Medial (static markers carried by the thigh-cluster rigid fit); ankle = midpoint of Ankle and Ankle.Medial (shank-cluster fit)
method.foot: toe tip = Heel.Bottom + 1.5 (MT1/MT5 midpoint - Heel.Bottom); foot centre 0.44 of the way heel to toe tip (0.66 of heel to MT midpoint); foot length heel to toe tip; a single MT marker is used when the other is missing
method.inertia: de Leva 1996 male set for all subjects (the one woman too): thigh 0.1416 / 0.4095 / 0.329, shank 0.0433 / 0.4459 / 0.255, foot 0.0137 / 0.44 / 0.257 (mass fraction / COM from proximal / gyration radius, fractions of length); segment lengths per frame in the sagittal plane
method.hat: point mass 0.6028 of body mass at the midpoint of the two hip joint centres + (dx, dy), dy = 0.18 x height, dx = dy tan(lean); no rotation; leans 0, 5, 10 deg and a per-speed best fit
method.bestLean: tan(lean) = mean stance offset of the force line from the lean-0 COM / (HAT fraction x dy), per subject and speed; the speed value is the mean over the 28 subjects; offset = (x_cop - x_com) + (Fx/Fy) y_com, i.e. the horizontal distance of the force line from the COM at COM height
method.sign: H z component anticlockwise positive; torque of the ground force about the COM = (x_cop - x_com) Fy + y_com Fx = m dH/dt (numerical check in checks.torqueSign)
method.predictions: A: Fx = -(x_cop - x_hip) Fy / y_hip (stance hip joint centre); B: same with the COM; C: Fx = (m dH/dt - (x_cop - x_com) Fy) / y_com; compared in body weights over 10-90 % of stance where Fy >= 0.2 BW
method.filtering: markers 15 Hz zero-lag 2nd-order Butterworth (as landing-fukuchi.js); velocities and accelerations by central differences at 150 Hz (a = x[k+1] - 2x[k] + x[k-1]); forces 30 Hz zero-lag, per contact for stance curves (COP held where Fy < 0.2 BW before filtering) and over the whole record for stride-wide plate series
method.plate: aComY_plate = Fy/m - g; aComX_plate = Fx/m; plate-derived COM vx and y are periodic (mean acceleration removed, mean velocity zero) over the stride; vxPlateRel is the integral of Fx/m from strike
method.stances: stance = raw 20 N strike to toe-off; stance curves at 0, 5 ... 100 % (cubic interpolation of 150 Hz series, linear for forces); stride curves at 0 ... 100 % of the stride (strike to next strike of the same leg)
method.pelvis: tilt = angle of the mid-ASIS - mid-PSIS line in the sagittal plane, positive = anterior tilt (ASIS below PSIS); rotation = angle of the left-to-right ASIS line seen from above, positive when the right ASIS is ahead; rotStance flips the sign for left-stance strides so that positive = stance-side hip forward
method.cohorts: strides -> legs -> subjects as in landing-fukuchi.js; rearfoot = legs whose RFSI/LFSI is "Rearfoot"

torqueSign.note: pooled valid stance frames, lean 0: measured torque of the ground force about the COM = (x_cop - x_com) Fy + y_com Fx (per kg) regressed on model dH/dt; sign is right if the slope is positive and near 1
